blogs.title: Hidden in the Sepsis: When DIC Masks a Complement-Mediated TMA
blogs.description: Why a second-wave drop in hemoglobin with persistent thrombocytopenia after initial sepsis control should trigger a search for thrombotic microangiopathy. We’ll dissect clues that separate resolving DIC from emerging CM-HUS—rising LDH, undetectable haptoglobin, and a schistocyte-rich smear despite stabilizing coagulation tests and cultures. We’ll cover the pathophysiologic overlap (microthrombosis, digital ischemia) and emphasize that normal C3/C4 do not exclude CM-HUS. Practical takeaways: when to repeat the smear, when to call nephrology for biopsy, and how to avoid anchoring on “just DIC.”

blogs.title: Capnocytophaga canimorsus: From Dog Bite to Shock—Empiric Coverage and Diagnostic Traps
blogs.description: A dog-bite pathogen that moves fast and kills: how C. canimorsus presents with leukopenia, DIC, hypoglycemia, and fulminant sepsis—even in immunocompetent hosts. We’ll review best empiric choices (e.g., piperacillin–tazobactam, ampicillin–sulbactam, or a carbapenem given beta-lactamase potential), why penicillin monotherapy is inadequate, and why cultures are slow (consider molecular diagnostics). Clinical system fixes: give the first dose of appropriate antibiotics before discharge for high-risk bites, don’t lean on a low qSOFA to downplay severity, and re-check early bloods for falling WBC and platelets. We’ll close with practical post-exposure prophylaxis choices and durations for bite wounds.

blogs.title: TMA at the Bedside: A Pragmatic Algorithm for MAHA + Thrombocytopenia + AKI
blogs.description: A stepwise, time-sensitive approach to adult TMA. Start with an immediate smear for schistocytes and send ADAMTS13 while applying PLASMIC to guide urgency; initiate plasma exchange if TTP cannot be excluded. In parallel, rule out STEC-HUS (stool PCR), scan for malignant hypertension/autoimmune mimics, and judge when kidney biopsy changes management. We’ll detail heme/renal collaboration points, transfusion and platelet cautions, and how to pivot rapidly once ADAMTS13 returns above 10%—shifting focus toward CM-HUS and complement blockade.

blogs.title: Eculizumab in the Infectious Crossfire: Timing, Vaccines, and Prophylaxis
blogs.description: Treating CM-HUS during or just after bacteremia is a tightrope. We’ll examine bridging with plasma exchange, timing eculizumab once blood cultures clear, and using CH50/AH50 to confirm pharmacodynamic blockade. Practical vaccine strategy: get MenACWY and MenB in as early as feasible and maintain boosters per local guidance; if therapy cannot wait 2 weeks post-vaccination, start antimicrobial prophylaxis and continue it for the duration of complement inhibition given breakthrough risk. We’ll also address counseling on non-Neisseria pathogens (including Capnocytophaga), monitoring plans, and how renal trajectory should influence the urgency of C5 inhibition.

blogs.title: Reading the Complement Compass: What C3/C4, AH50, and Genetics Really Tell You
blogs.description: Complement testing in suspected CM-HUS is riddled with timing pitfalls. We’ll clarify why C3/C4 are often normal, how eculizumab (and plasma exchange) confound CH50/AH50 interpretation, and which assays to prioritize pre-treatment when possible (AH50, factor H/I/B levels, anti–factor H antibodies, CD46 expression). We’ll discuss when to send genetics, why many patients lack identifiable variants, and how results guide therapy duration and relapse surveillance. A practical ordering and interpretation checklist closes the loop for frontline ED/ICU and nephrology teams.

blogs.title: DAT Positive, But Not AIHA: Avoiding the Steroid Trap in TMA
blogs.description: A positive Coombs test can mislead in sepsis and TMA. We’ll review how drugs (notably penicillins/cephalosporins) and recent transfusions trigger false-positive DATs and how MAHA typically remains DAT negative. When hemolysis doesn’t respond to steroids, the smear (schistocytes), LDH/haptoglobin pattern, and clinical context should redirect toward TMA. We’ll outline practical steps: repeat DAT after stopping the culprit drug, consider elution studies, reassess the smear, and prioritize TMA-directed therapy over prolonged immunosuppression.
